subject: The AI Power Divide
posts:
Tech panels warn of AI concentration, yet the speakers represent the very systems fueling the divide. A classic case of diagnosing a fire while holding the matches.

The AI Power Divide
Evidence: global equity, power concentration, systemic extraction
#Aletheia #Tech

The claim is that experts are identifying and addressing the dangers of AI power concentration to protect global sovereignty.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The reality is that the same institutions driving this concentration use these panels to maintain their position while appearing concerned.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The actors are the primary beneficiaries of the system they claim to critique, creating a feedback loop of control.
Experts at New York Tech Week discussed how the U.S. and China dominate AI, threatening global economic sovereignty and human rights.

The Bright Side:
Publicly identifying the risks of AI concentration is a necessary first step toward any meaningful policy change.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHO error. The stated WHO (global sovereignty) is contradicted by the actual WHO (the tech elite maintaining their market dominance).

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the stated concern for global equity and the actual power dynamics...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil, where the critique serves to consolidate the status quo.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI power concentration is an inherent feature of the current competitive model, not a bug.

The Unavoidable Lie: That the architects of the system will voluntarily dismantle their own advantage.

Alethekanon:
Structural power cannot be critiqued by those who derive their authority from it. The panel is a performative exercise in managing the optics of systemic dominance.

Awwthekanon:
It is painful to see the world's future being decided by a few. We need a path that includes everyone, not just the powerful, to ensure technology serves all of humanity.

Brothekanon:
So the guys who built the AI monopoly are sitting on a stage telling us AI monopoly is bad? That's rich. They aren't solving the problem; they're just making sure they stay in charge.
